scene.label: Act 4, Scene 5
scene.title: SCENE V. A room in the Garter Inn
scene.location: A room in the Garter Inn

lines.text: What wouldst thou have, boor? What, thick-skin? Speak, breathe, discuss; brief, short, quick, snap.
lines.plainText: What wouldst thou have boor What thickskin Speak breathe discuss brief short quick snap

lines.text: Marry, sir, I come to speak with Sir John Falstaff from Master Slender.
lines.plainText: Marry sir I come to speak with Sir John Falstaff from Master Slender

lines.text: There's his chamber, his house, his castle, his standing-bed and truckle-bed. 'Tis painted about with the story of the Prodigal, fresh and new. Go, knock and call. He'll speak like an Anthropophaginian unto thee. Knock, I say.
lines.plainText: There's his chamber his house his castle his standingbed and trucklebed 'Tis painted about with the story of the Prodigal fresh and new Go knock and call He'll speak like an Anthropophaginian unto thee Knock I say

lines.text: There's an old woman, a fat woman, gone up into his chamber. I'll be so bold as stay, sir, till she come down. I come to speak with her, indeed.
lines.plainText: There's an old woman a fat woman gone up into his chamber I'll be so bold as stay sir till she come down I come to speak with her indeed

lines.text: Ha? A fat woman? The knight may be robbed. I'll call.—Bully knight! Bully Sir John! Speak from thy lungs military. Art thou there? It is thine host, thine Ephesian, calls.
lines.plainText: Ha A fat woman The knight may be robbed I'll callBully knight Bully Sir John Speak from thy lungs military Art thou there It is thine host thine Ephesian calls

lines.text: [Above.] How now, mine host?
lines.plainText: Above How now mine host

lines.text: Here's a Bohemian-Tartar tarries the coming down of thy fat woman. Let her descend, bully, let her descend. My chambers are honourable. Fie! Privacy? Fie!
lines.plainText: Here's a BohemianTartar tarries the coming down of thy fat woman Let her descend bully let her descend My chambers are honourable Fie Privacy Fie

lines.text: There was, mine host, an old fat woman even now with me, but she's gone.
lines.plainText: There was mine host an old fat woman even now with me but she's gone

lines.text: Pray you, sir, was't not the wise woman of Brentford?
lines.plainText: Pray you sir was't not the wise woman of Brentford

lines.text: Ay, marry was it, mussel-shell. What would you with her?
lines.plainText: Ay marry was it musselshell What would you with her

lines.text: My master, sir, my Master Slender, sent to her, seeing her go through the streets, to know, sir, whether one Nym, sir, that beguiled him of a chain, had the chain or no.
lines.plainText: My master sir my Master Slender sent to her seeing her go through the streets to know sir whether one Nym sir that beguiled him of a chain had the chain or no

lines.text: I spake with the old woman about it.
lines.plainText: I spake with the old woman about it

lines.text: And what says she, I pray, sir?
lines.plainText: And what says she I pray sir

lines.text: Marry, she says that the very same man that beguiled Master Slender of his chain cozened him of it.
lines.plainText: Marry she says that the very same man that beguiled Master Slender of his chain cozened him of it

lines.text: I would I could have spoken with the woman herself. I had other things to have spoken with her too, from him.
lines.plainText: I would I could have spoken with the woman herself I had other things to have spoken with her too from him

lines.text: What are they? Let us know.
lines.plainText: What are they Let us know

lines.text: Ay, come. Quick.
lines.plainText: Ay come Quick

lines.text: I may not conceal them, sir.
lines.plainText: I may not conceal them sir

lines.text: Conceal them, or thou diest.
lines.plainText: Conceal them or thou diest

lines.text: Why, sir, they were nothing but about Mistress Anne Page, to know if it were my master's fortune to have her or no.
lines.plainText: Why sir they were nothing but about Mistress Anne Page to know if it were my master's fortune to have her or no

lines.text: 'Tis, 'tis his fortune.
lines.plainText: 'Tis 'tis his fortune

lines.text: What sir?
lines.plainText: What sir

lines.text: To have her, or no. Go, say the woman told me so.
lines.plainText: To have her or no Go say the woman told me so

lines.text: May I be bold to say so, sir?
lines.plainText: May I be bold to say so sir

lines.text: Ay, sir; like who more bold?
lines.plainText: Ay sir like who more bold

lines.text: I thank your worship; I shall make my master glad with these tidings.
lines.plainText: I thank your worship I shall make my master glad with these tidings

lines.text: Thou art clerkly, thou art clerkly, Sir John. Was there a wise woman with thee?
lines.plainText: Thou art clerkly thou art clerkly Sir John Was there a wise woman with thee

lines.text: Ay, that there was, mine host; one that hath taught me more wit than ever I learned before in my life; and I paid nothing for it neither, but was paid for my learning.
lines.plainText: Ay that there was mine host one that hath taught me more wit than ever I learned before in my life and I paid nothing for it neither but was paid for my learning

lines.text: Out, alas, sir, cozenage, mere cozenage!
lines.plainText: Out alas sir cozenage mere cozenage

lines.text: Where be my horses? Speak well of them, varletto.
lines.plainText: Where be my horses Speak well of them varletto

lines.text: Run away, with the cozeners. For so soon as I came beyond Eton, they threw me off from behind one of them, in a slough of mire, and set spurs and away, like three German devils, three Doctor Faustuses.
lines.plainText: Run away with the cozeners For so soon as I came beyond Eton they threw me off from behind one of them in a slough of mire and set spurs and away like three German devils three Doctor Faustuses

lines.text: They are gone but to meet the Duke, villain, do not say they be fled. Germans are honest men.
lines.plainText: They are gone but to meet the Duke villain do not say they be fled Germans are honest men

lines.text: Where is mine host?
lines.plainText: Where is mine host

lines.text: What is the matter, sir?
lines.plainText: What is the matter sir

lines.text: Have a care of your entertainments. There is a friend of mine come to town tells me there is three cozen-Germans that has cozened all the hosts of Readings, of Maidenhead, of Colebrook, of horses and money. I tell you for good will, look you. You are wise, and full of gibes and vlouting-stocks, and 'tis not convenient you should be cozened. Fare you well.
lines.plainText: Have a care of your entertainments There is a friend of mine come to town tells me there is three cozenGermans that has cozened all the hosts of Readings of Maidenhead of Colebrook of horses and money I tell you for good will look you You are wise and full of gibes and vloutingstocks and 'tis not convenient you should be cozened Fare you well

lines.text: Vere is mine host de Jarteer?
lines.plainText: Vere is mine host de Jarteer

lines.text: Here, Master Doctor, in perplexity and doubtful dilemma.
lines.plainText: Here Master Doctor in perplexity and doubtful dilemma

lines.text: I cannot tell vat is dat, but it is tell-a me dat you make grand preparation for a Duke de Jamany. By my trot, dere is no duke that the court is know to come. I tell you for good will. Adieu.
lines.plainText: I cannot tell vat is dat but it is tella me dat you make grand preparation for a Duke de Jamany By my trot dere is no duke that the court is know to come I tell you for good will Adieu

lines.text: Hue and cry, villain, go!—Assist me, knight, I am undone.—Fly, run, hue and cry, villain, I am undone!
lines.plainText: Hue and cry villain goAssist me knight I am undoneFly run hue and cry villain I am undone

lines.text: I would all the world might be cozened, for I have been cozened and beaten too. If it should come to the ear of the court how I have been transformed, and how my transformation hath been washed and cudgelled, they would melt me out of my fat drop by drop, and liquor fishermen's boots with me. I warrant they would whip me with their fine wits till I were as crestfallen as a dried pear. I never prospered since I forswore myself at primero. Well, if my wind were but long enough, I would repent.
lines.plainText: I would all the world might be cozened for I have been cozened and beaten too If it should come to the ear of the court how I have been transformed and how my transformation hath been washed and cudgelled they would melt me out of my fat drop by drop and liquor fishermen's boots with me I warrant they would whip me with their fine wits till I were as crestfallen as a dried pear I never prospered since I forswore myself at primero Well if my wind were but long enough I would repent

lines.text: From the two parties, forsooth.
lines.plainText: From the two parties forsooth

lines.text: The devil take one party and his dam the other, and so they shall be both bestowed. I have suffered more for their sakes, more than the villainous inconstancy of man's disposition is able to bear.
lines.plainText: The devil take one party and his dam the other and so they shall be both bestowed I have suffered more for their sakes more than the villainous inconstancy of man's disposition is able to bear

lines.text: And have not they suffered? Yes, I warrant, speciously one of them. Mistress Ford, good heart, is beaten black and blue, that you cannot see a white spot about her.
lines.plainText: And have not they suffered Yes I warrant speciously one of them Mistress Ford good heart is beaten black and blue that you cannot see a white spot about her

lines.text: What tellst thou me of black and blue? I was beaten myself into all the colours of the rainbow, and was like to be apprehended for the witch of Brentford. But that my admirable dexterity of wit, my counterfeiting the action of an old woman, delivered me, the knave constable had set me i' the stocks, i' the common stocks, for a witch.
lines.plainText: What tellst thou me of black and blue I was beaten myself into all the colours of the rainbow and was like to be apprehended for the witch of Brentford But that my admirable dexterity of wit my counterfeiting the action of an old woman delivered me the knave constable had set me i' the stocks i' the common stocks for a witch

lines.text: Sir, let me speak with you in your chamber, you shall hear how things go, and, I warrant, to your content. Here is a letter will say somewhat. Good hearts, what ado here is to bring you together! Sure, one of you does not serve heaven well, that you are so crossed.
lines.plainText: Sir let me speak with you in your chamber you shall hear how things go and I warrant to your content Here is a letter will say somewhat Good hearts what ado here is to bring you together Sure one of you does not serve heaven well that you are so crossed

lines.text: Come up into my chamber.
lines.plainText: Come up into my chamber
